name: Secrets CLI (agent-safe surface)
purpose: The command-line surface every agent, operator, and CI job uses when working with secrets. Keeps secret material off argv, off logs, off structured output, and off terminal echoes captured by an agent transcript. Its structured output surface is also the field contract the optional admin-UI Secrets page renders against.
responsibilities: Expose `list`, `read <name>`, `put <name>`, `reflect`, `rotate <name>`, `verify` verbs; each verb enforces the value-off-argv and value-off-log rules regardless of how it is invoked (AC-8105-1, AC-8105-2).
Refuse to print a secret value to a TTY without an explicit `--show` flag; the flag is honoured only when stdout is a TTY, deliberately excluding scripted transcript capture (AC-8105-1).
Refuse a value passed as a positional argument or as an option value with `SECRETS_VALUE_ON_ARGV_REFUSED`; require `put` to read the value from stdin (AC-8105-2).

Emit a structured `--json` and `--report` output surface whose entries carry `name`, `environment`, `owner`, `rotationDays`, `lastRotatedAt`, and `required`; never a `value` or a hash of it (AC-8105-3, AC-8110-2).
Wrap the CLI's own logger in a redactor that replaces any bytes matching a resolved secret value with a fixed-length placeholder before writing to any log sink (AC-8105-4).
Serve as the field contract for the optional admin-UI Secrets page: the page renders the same field set the `--json` surface carries and adds no value-carrying cell (AC-8110-2).
internalStructure: One CLI module with per-verb handlers. Composes TAC-901 (client), TAC-902 (manifest), TAC-903 (reflector), TAC-904 (rotation gate). A shared redactor middleware wraps every log-emit point; a shared TTY/argv guard middleware runs before every verb's handler.

interfaces.name: process
interfaces.description: The host process's argv, stdin, stdout, stderr, and env; the CLI reads argv and stdin, writes to stdout and stderr, and reads a small allow-listed env slice (audit principal id, active environment).

interfaces.name: logSink
interfaces.description: The CLI's own log destination (stderr by default; a file when `--log-file` is set); every write passes through the redactor.

dependencies.name: Rotation gate
dependencies.description: Backing implementation for the `verify` verb when scoped to rotation checks.

tradeoffs: The `--show` flag gated on a TTY closes the common agent-transcript leak but does not stop a human copying a value from their own terminal into a screenshot; nothing at the CLI layer can. Projects that need a harder gate override with a project-level ADR requiring an out-of-band value delivery (a browser paste-buffer with clipboard auto-clear, a hardware-token flow), and this CLI becomes read-only-metadata plus the piped-stdin `put`.
